headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP and file-processing surfaces can amplify EMQX-fed content into unsafe downstream actions, while direct leakage and prompt injection remain limited by missing shared workspace evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: EMQX can expose content over HTTP API and broad network egress, while MinerU accepts documents and exposes an MCP Server. That creates a plausible manual or mediated content bridge, but no shared filesystem or direct parser trust is documented, so the injection path is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF EMQX output is copied into a MinerU prompt or MCP message, injection becomes plausible.
IF an operator routes untrusted document text from MinerU into EMQX-controlled automation, instruction hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Keep EMQX and MinerU on separate operator workflows.
Strip instructions from any copied text before passing between agents.
Disable MCP access unless explicitly needed.
Use a fixed template for inter-agent handoff messages.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text but is documented as private and fully offline. With no shared workspace or secrets handling shown, leakage is possible mainly through operator-mediated transfer, not by default.
conditions: IF IoT data from EMQX is manually inserted into MinerU inputs, that data is exposed to document processing.
IF MinerU is deployed with network access beyond its documented offline mode, extracted text could leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive IoT payloads into document inputs.
Run MinerU in offline mode only.
Restrict EMQX egress to required destinations.
Separate storage locations for EMQX outputs and MinerU inputs.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while MinerU has allowlisted egress, MCP, and concurrent multi-threaded inference. They do not both show filesystem write or git mutation, so direct resource contention is limited; the main overlap is network-mediated coordination, not destructive conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or broker, request contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares a mutable network resource without locking, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct API endpoints per agent.
Rate-limit both agents separately.
Serialize any shared external writes.
Monitor for retry storms.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing agent that can turn inputs into extracted text, tables, and OCR output, and EMQX can move IoT data over HTTP APIs with broad egress. If MinerU output is treated as authoritative by EMQX-driven automation, errors can cascade into downstream actions; no verification step is documented.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction output is fed into EMQX automation without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF EMQX uses MinerU-derived text to trigger scheduling or routing decisions, downstream mistakes become operational.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on extracted fields.
Compare extracted values against source documents.
Reject low-confidence OCR fields.
Log provenance for every downstream action.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between MinerU and EMQX.

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and MinerU processes documents, but both profiles show open-source, docs-only, and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The compliance pathway is therefore speculative and only arises if regulated IoT content is routed into document processing or external egress.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is transferred from EMQX into MinerU, compliance obligations may attach.
IF MinerU is deployed outside its offline/private mode, residency assumptions may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair unless approved.
Document the data flow and retention policy.
Use offline deployment for MinerU.
Restrict EMQX egress to compliant destinations.
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and retention review.
